issues.title: [1.21.x] es_es.json is invalid JSON (missing comma), and V2-deprecated toast references undefined translation keys
issues.body:
Two separate issues on the `1.21.9` branch (the line that `modmenu-16.0.1` for MC 1.21.10 is built from). Both are already resolved on `26.x`, so this is only about the 1.21.x maintenance line.

---

## 1. `es_es.json` is invalid JSON — the whole Spanish translation fails to load

`src/main/resources/assets/modmenu/lang/es_es.json` is missing a comma after line 172:

```json
   171:   "option.modmenu.button_update_badge.true": "SÍ",
   172:   "option.modmenu.button_update_badge.false": "NO"     <-- comma missing
   173:   "option.modmenu.quick_configure": "Configuración rápida",
   174:   "option.modmenu.quick_configure.true": "SÍ",
```

A parser stops at line 173 col 3 with `Expecting ',' delimiter`. Because a language file is one JSON object, a structural error like this doesn't degrade gracefully — the whole file fails, so Spanish users get English for all of Mod Menu rather than losing a single string.

Worth noting Gson's lenient mode doesn't rescue this. Leniency covers comments, single quotes and unquoted names, but a missing separator between object members still fails ("Unterminated object"), so this isn't one of the cases MC tolerates.

**Caveat on my end:** I verified the file is invalid JSON, but I play in English and haven't watched it fail in-game, so I haven't observed the user-facing symptom directly.

**Status across branches:**

| branch | `es_es.json` |
|---|---|
| `1.21.9` | **invalid** (line 173) |
| `26.1` | valid |
| `26.2` | valid |
| `26.4` (default) | valid |

So it looks like the fix landed on the 26.x line and wasn't backported.

Possibly adjacent to #355 ("Duplicate current spanish translation"), which is open — that one is about duplicated entries rather than a syntax error, so I filed separately, but if you're touching `es_es.json` anyway they may be worth doing together.

---

## 2. V2-deprecated toast shows raw translation keys

`UpdateCheckerUtil.triggerV2DeprecatedToast()` builds a `SystemToast` from two keys that don't exist in `en_us.json`:

```java
// src/main/java/com/terraformersmc/modmenu/util/UpdateCheckerUtil.java:160-165
public static void triggerV2DeprecatedToast() {
    if (modrinthApiV2Deprecated && ModMenuConfig.UPDATE_CHECKER.getValue()) {
        MinecraftClient.getInstance().getToastManager().add(new SystemToast(SystemToast.Type.PERIODIC_NOTIFICATION,
            Text.translatable("modmenu.modrinth.v2_deprecated.title"),
            Text.translatable("modmenu.modrinth.v2_deprecated.description")
        ));
    }
}
```

The only `modmenu.modrinth`-prefixed key in `en_us.json` on this branch is `modmenu.modrinth` itself (`"Modrinth"`). Neither `…v2_deprecated.title` nor `…v2_deprecated.description` is defined — I also checked `de_de` and the shipped `modmenu-16.0.1.jar`, same result.

So whenever Modrinth's v2 API is flagged deprecated and the update checker is on, the toast renders the literal strings `modmenu.modrinth.v2_deprecated.title` / `modmenu.modrinth.v2_deprecated.description` instead of readable text.

This is gone on `26.4` — `triggerV2DeprecatedToast` and the keys don't appear there at all, so the code was removed rather than the strings added. Either backporting that removal or adding the two keys would fix it.

---

### How these were found

Two static passes over my installed mods:

1. Extracted the `CONSTANT_Utf8` pool from every `.class` file, kept strings shaped like translation keys whose namespace matches one of the mod's own lang namespaces, and diffed against `en_us.json`. That surfaced issue 2. (It also flagged `sodium.codegen.dump` and `sodium.debug.shaders.dump` in Sodium, which are system property names rather than translation keys — false positives, not reported.)
2. Parsed all 154 of Mod Menu's language files; `es_es.json` was the only one that failed.

issues.title: Cloth Config labels show translation keys (e.g. text.cloth-config.reset_value) when using Mod Menu 17.0.0‑beta.2
issues.body: Bug description Cloth Config labels are not translated when opening mod configuration screens via Mod Menu 17.0.0‑beta.2. Instead of localized text, raw translation keys are displayed (for example: text.cloth-config.reset_value). This affects configuration screens for mods such as BetterF3, which rely on Cloth Config. Is this a crash? No — UI / localization issue. How can you reproduce it? Launch Minecraft 1.21.11 with Fabric. Install: Mod Menu 17.0.0‑beta.2 Cloth Config 21.11.153 BetterF3 17.0.0 (or another mod using Cloth Config) Open Mod Menu. Click the config button for the mod. Observe untranslated labels, e.g.: text.cloth-config.reset_value What other mods is this issue happening with? Observed with: BetterF3 17.0.0 Likely affects any mod using Cloth Config when opened through Mod Menu. Does this happen when only this mod is installed? Requires: Mod Menu 17.0.0‑beta.2 Cloth Config A mod providing a Cloth Config screen If Mod Menu is removed and configs are opened in‑game instead, translations display correctly. issues.body:
## [1.21.10] Game Crash When Loading Modmenu Alone (fabric-screen-api-v1 Mixin Injection Failure)

### Environment Information
- Minecraft Version: 1.21.10
- Fabric Loader Version: 0.18.3
- Modmenu Version: 17.0.0-alpha.1
- Java Version: Java 21
- Operating System: Windows 11 Pro 64-bit (10.0, Build 26200) (26100.ge_release.240331-1435)
- Number of Loaded Mods: Only Modmenu、Fabric API、Text Placeholder API (Mod Support Library)
- Processor: 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12450H (12 CPUs), ~2.0GHz
- Memory: 16384MB RAM
- Card name: Intel(R) UHD Graphics

### Description
After installing the Modmenu mod alone and launching the game, a crash is triggered immediately. The core cause of the crash is a failed Mixin injection from the `fabric-screen-api-v1` mod, which cannot find the target method `method_25423(II)V`. The game launches normally after removing Modmenu, confirming the issue is solely caused by the Modmenu mod.

### Reproduction Steps
1. Install Minecraft 1.21.10 with Fabric Loader 0.18.3.(Possess the Fabric API)
2. Install Modmenu and its prerequisite libraries
3. Launch the game, which triggers a crash with repeated Mixin injection failure errors in the log.

### Core Error Log Snippet (Formatted Code Block)
```
[14:18:10] [Datafixer Bootstrap/ERROR]: Mixin apply for mod fabric-screen-api-v1 failed fabric-screen-api-v1.mixins.json:ScreenMixin from mod fabric-screen-api-v1 -> net.minecraft.class_437: org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.injection.throwables.InvalidInjectionException Critical injection failure: @Inject annotation on beforeInitScreen could not find any targets matching 'method_25423(II)V' in net/minecraft/class_437. No refMap loaded. org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.injection.throwables.InvalidInjectionException: Critical injection failure: @Inject annotation on beforeInitScreen could not find any targets matching 'method_25423(II)V' in net/minecraft/class_437. No refMap loaded.
```


### Actual Behavior
The game crashes immediately on launch. The log repeatedly outputs the aforementioned Mixin injection failure error, preventing access to the game's main menu.

The button opens the `mods` folder within the current game directory, but that's not guaranteed to be the actual mods folder. - https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/blob/438d16e69ad40962a12ead6bdb5acc1a42857bcb/src/main/java/com/terraformersmc/modmenu/gui/ModsScreen.java#L236

fabric-loader will set the mods folder location according to the `fabric.modsFolder` system property - https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric-loader/blob/8fc5065227f72b5a00ae4c0376398120776926a9/src/main/java/net/fabricmc/loader/impl/util/SystemProperties.java#L47

Unfortunately fabric-loader does not expose a method in its API to get the mods folder, but modmenu could also read the system property.

issues.title: [1.21.3] Mods will have an non-functional config button when `ModMenuApi#getModConfigScreenFactory` is not implemented.
issues.body:
In my mod Configured, I only provide config screens for other mods using `ModMenuApi#getProvidedConfigScreenFactories`, I do not provide one to the mod itself.  However, as of https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/commit/4fd1eb7fe056dc89656bc6a93363fd73070a6a9b and https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/commit/39f0fcf8d01cecdce08505a4ee748f08abd9cb6f, ModMenu will now believe that Configured itself has a config and will show a config button that is non-functional when clicked. My implementation of `ModMenuApi#getProvidedConfigScreenFactories` has also explicitly ensured that a config screen is not [provided by itself](https://github.com/MrCrayfish/Configured/blob/22cb06904e33f78a088edf80ccdb321e41c6d5aa/fabric/src/main/java/com/mrcrayfish/configured/integration/ModMenuConfigFactory.java#L31).

Solution, default implementation of `getModConfigScreenFactory` should return `null` instead of an empty factory, then check for `null` before putting into `ModMenu#configScreenFactories` map. I am not sure what implications this will have changing the default implementation, but I don't see another way to detect if a mod has a config screen without an expensive to `ConfigScreenFactory#create`.

The following screenshots are taken while opening the menu in the title screen.
Before:
![Memory usage before opening Mods menu: around 2700 MB](https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/assets/49392266/511e3860-2bc3-414c-9daf-e1c62500cb73)

After:

After Minecraft unfreezes and the memory spike is over, the JVM seems allocate 1GB more than before, idling at 3664 MB compared to 2693 MB.
If allowed to reach the memory cap, the freeze and memory spike will take longer.

On one occasion I have managed to cause Minecraft to crash due to a lack of available memory, but I cannot reproduce this again.

issues.title: Author order is not preserved in the credits list
issues.body:
As of #706, credits for Fabric mods now separate by authors and contributors, with each list being sorted alphabetically.

However, authors are often listed in a particular order, meaning that the primary author of a mod may be sorted after its secondary authors. This behavior is also inconsistent with the order shown in the authors list next to the icon.

To keep the intent of the authors list, I believe that authors should not be sorted within the credits.

issues.title: Undocumented behaviour of `ModMenuApi#getModConfigScreenFactory()`
issues.body:
I was brought to attention that `ModMenuApi#getModConfigScreenFactory()` is able to return `null` (the factory itself, not the value created by it). This is not mentioned in the method documentation or annotated. 

A null check is performed here when retrieving the factory from the map, but is this to allow the mentioned method to return null or is this just a standard null check after getting a value from a map?
https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/blob/1.20.3/src/main/java/com/terraformersmc/modmenu/ModMenu.java#L61-L62 

The factory is pushed to the map even if it is `null`.
https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/blob/1.20.3/src/main/java/com/terraformersmc/modmenu/ModMenu.java#L80

I am not sure right now if this is intended or is being confused with the return value of `ConfigScreenFactory#create`.

issues.title: Modmenu produces a NPE when having an unknown Badge entry
issues.body:
Having a mod that has for example the following entry in the `fabric.mod.json` lets modmenu produce a NPE while rendering badges.
```json
"custom": {
    "modmenu": {
      "badges": [
        "liteloader"
      ]
    }
  }
```
This occours, because the `badge` variable in the second method here is `null`:
https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/blob/5d640d66a3e182889f84075d8fded0470534dbf5/src/main/java/com/terraformersmc/modmenu/util/mod/ModBadgeRenderer.java#L31-L40
This happens because the `Set<Badge>` contains `null`. After looking from where this set comes, you get to here:
https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/blob/5d640d66a3e182889f84075d8fded0470534dbf5/src/main/java/com/terraformersmc/modmenu/util/mod/fabric/FabricMod.java#L92-L131
As you can see, in Line 113 it sets the field `this.badges`, which is returned by the `getBadges` method. As you can see, this code doesn't directly add `null` as a value. Therefore, the value `null` must come from the field `modMenuData.badges`. This field is set in the constructor of `ModMenuData`:
https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/blob/5d640d66a3e182889f84075d8fded0470534dbf5/src/main/java/com/terraformersmc/modmenu/util/mod/fabric/FabricMod.java#L337-L341
This just calls `Badges.convert()`, which takes a `Set<String>` and gives back a `Set<Badge>`:
https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/blob/5d640d66a3e182889f84075d8fded0470534dbf5/src/main/java/com/terraformersmc/modmenu/util/mod/Mod.java#L151-L153
And this also shows us where the `null` comes from: `KEY_MAP::get` can return `null` if there's no key-value pair. And that's percisely what happens in my case.

Note that the usage of `liteloader` here is just because it happened in a modmenu port to [Ornithe](https://github.com/OrnitheMC), a modding toolchain for old minecraft versions. The relevant code path was not changed in the code. Therefore it could also happen in modern modmenu.
(I also fist asked there, <https://github.com/OrnitheMC/modmenu/issues/4>, and we determined that upstream also has the issue, and therefore I think that it should be fixed in upstream)

A crashlog from Ornithe:
```txt
Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException
	at com.terraformersmc.modmenu.util.mod.ModBadgeRenderer.drawBadge(ModBadgeRenderer.java:33) ~[modmenu-0.2.0+mc1.12.2.jar:?]
	at com.terraformersmc.modmenu.util.mod.ModBadgeRenderer.lambda$draw$0(ModBadgeRenderer.java:29) ~[modmenu-0.2.0+mc1.12.2.jar:?]
	at java.lang.Iterable.forEach(Iterable.java:75) ~[?:1.8.0_392]
	at com.terraformersmc.modmenu.util.mod.ModBadgeRenderer.draw(ModBadgeRenderer.java:29) ~[modmenu-0.2.0+mc1.12.2.jar:?]
	at com.terraformersmc.modmenu.gui.widget.entries.ModListEntry.render(ModListEntry.java:75) ~[modmenu-0.2.0+mc1.12.2.jar:?]
	at net.minecraft.client.gui.widget.EntryListWidget.renderEntry(EntryListWidget.java:28) ~[1.12.2-TRv0.8.2-named-711666161528F3329D7A8C8C611232C03E2D58B845ABA1B8F40897F5800EAE50.jar:?]
	at com.terraformersmc.modmenu.gui.widget.ModListWidget.renderList(ModListWidget.java:246) ~[modmenu-0.2.0+mc1.12.2.jar:?]
	at net.minecraft.client.gui.widget.ListWidget.render(ListWidget.java:194) ~[1.12.2-TRv0.8.2-named-711666161528F3329D7A8C8C611232C03E2D58B845ABA1B8F40897F5800EAE50.jar:?]
	at com.terraformersmc.modmenu.gui.ModsScreen.render(ModsScreen.java:321) ~[modmenu-0.2.0+mc1.12.2.jar:?]
	at net.minecraft.client.render.GameRenderer.render(GameRenderer.java:947) ~[1.12.2-TRv0.8.2-named-711666161528F3329D7A8C8C611232C03E2D58B845ABA1B8F40897F5800EAE50.jar:?]
	... 6 more
```

This issue also comes with further questions:
- Should there be some kind of API to register badge? This would, at least partially, remove the issue, as then one mod counld register the badge `liteloader` and define it's colors and text (see what skyrising used for an example here: <https://github.com/skyrising/ModMenu/commit/385c15f8197f83f0603ec23db98a1a6b00bd7a64>)
- This would however still not 100% fix the issue, `Badges.convert()` should at least either throw an exception if there's any `null` in the set (that could happen if a mod forgot to register a badge), or silently filter out `null`s in the set. This could be done by filtering the stream: `.filter(Objects::nonNull)`.

issues.title: Feature: V4V integration
issues.body:
It would be scope creep to ask this app to implement V4V boosting or streaming. Buut... It wouldn't be scope creep to allow developers to place a lightning network address inside their modmenu manifest.

- There's no existing app that could take advantage of this yet.
- However, minecraft modders are often grossly overworked, and undercompensated for their works. Actually... Nearly ALL FOSS devs are treated this way. This can't go on!
- Podcasting 2.0 is taking a brave new leap forward in a monetization strategy, built upon the best tech to do so. The tech is centered around the idea of: "how much value did my work give you?" -> "OK, if you can afford it: donate it back?".
- The issue mostly stems from gatekeeper payment entities that suck up too much of any given transaction to make this micro-donations worth anything for either party.
- All FOSS can take advantage of this.
   And all it would require from this mod to implement in the MC modding niche - is:
    - [ ] A valid manifest field with a lightning address in it. Accessible via an API.
    - [ ] (not sure if this' present currently) An API for adding buttons: (this would be leveraged by the V4V mod, not the individual mods themselves)
    e.g. [stream] -> modal asking for x SATS every y mins/hours/days/weeks used (all you would be doing is the button, not the streaming work)
    e.g. [boost] -> modal asking for a 1 time donation of x SATS allowing you to enter a custom message (feedback, etc))



# What is V4V?:
[reference 1](https://rss.com/blog/understanding-value-for-value-earn-bitcoin-from-your-podcast/)
[reference 2](https://www.fountain.fm/podcaster-guide)
[reference 3](https://value4value.info/)

issues.title: Suggestion: Sort by mods requiring an update
issues.body: I play with alot of mods like many others and I use the update badge feature to my mods. But since I have alot of mods, it is hard to sort through and find the mod that needs updating. Hence I propose a "Sort by Update" feature which only shows the mods that need updating.

issues.title: "Raised x Appleskin" fake update notification
issues.body:
Hello, I am using this mod

https://modrinth.com/mod/raised

And it has an additional which fixes a visual issue with the appleskin mod ( https://modrinth.com/mod/appleskin )

For some reason, this add on mod falsely shows a update indicator on the mod menu screen.

I am wondering if there is a feature I can use to clear this notification or disable update notifications for this specific mod without hiding it for all mods I have installed. Thank you.

issues.title: Mod Menu Update Checker not working correctly with quilt mods
issues.body: So I'm using quilt, I updated all my mods that the update checker said, I could update. But when I looked on the version for the update on simple voice chat, it was the same version that I had installed but for fabric, mine is for quilt. And I noticed that the quilt mods "Quilted Fabric API Quilt standard Libraries" and "Quilt Kotlin Libraries" weren't shown as updatable, but had some updates available as I checked on Modrinth.

issues.title: Crash trying to load v7.2.1 into 1.20.2-pre2
issues.body:
Just to clarify, i know ModMenu doesn't have an official build for 1.20.2-preX yet, but i tried to load it to see if the changes in vanilla would affect or not the mod, and if positive to gather the crash report to see if this would be of any use by your guys.

[Here's the crash i had.](https://gist.github.com/vico93/bb9b2d964236a22b4c72b3527f29155a)

I hope this can be of use on the process of updating the mod to 1.20.2!

issues.title: [Feature Request] Improved credits list
issues.body:
Currently the credits are just a list of all the authors and contributors' names all together. It would be great if this list could be broken down further into multiple lists based on the type of contributions.

i.e. "Authors", "Localization", "Texture", "Sound Design", "Contributors", "Supporters". Maybe also have other types like "Backers", "Subscribers", or "Patrons" for the people who want to include those.

I was thinking either keep them vertical as they are now, just with the list grouped by contribution, but maybe splitting it into columns would be a more effective use of space. Just something to consider.

![image](https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/assets/6429283/5d1443da-a86f-4f9d-8040-0abe7ac4d5c1)

issues.title: [Feat] Keep previous search result through GUI openings
issues.body:
I have been using mod menu in my custom modpacks since forever, there basically isn't a single modpack it isn't in.
I find myself opening and closing its interface quite often, especially when doing the last tidbits of in-game configuration.
It would be nice if, either as a config option or default behavior, mod menu kept the last search result when you close in and out of its interface.
(In between restarts would also be nice to have, but that sounds like a big hassle for not much, unless the foundations are already there)

issues.title: Badges for compatibility layer mods
issues.body:
ModMenu already seems to implement a [custom badge for mods patched using Patchwork](https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/blob/91460879c6d0693b14d1632baccea56bf3619f2e/src/main/java/com/terraformersmc/modmenu/util/mod/Mod.java#L123C4-L123C4). However when this change was made the badge was intended specifically for Patchwork rather than for any general purpose

This change would add a badge for each major mod loader that patchers or compatibility mods could use to tag their mods:

- `Badge.QUILT`
- `Badge.FORGE` (deprecates PATCHWORK_FORGE)

Additional badges would be added through the issue tracker [as requested in #191](https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/issues/191#issuecomment-770294015).

issues.title: Includes Fabric API & Floader Modules In Dev
issues.body:
It's really annoying, and I can't dev properly on Quilt while this is happening. I'm going to have to manually exclude it.

## Workaround
Include this exclusion in a block next to the inclusion of `modmenu` like this.
```kts
modRuntimeOnly("com.terraformersmc", "modmenu", "7.1.0") {
	exclude(group = "net.fabricmc.fabric-api")
	exclude(group = "net.fabricmc")
}
```

issues.title: Some issues with narrators
issues.body:
In the mod menu screen, the narrator has several problems (I'm in 1.19.4 Fabric 6.1.0-rc4):
- When using the keyboard to select some mods or buttons, the narrator may read "search for mods text field", instead of the information of that mod or buttons.
- When selecting a mod, the narrator does not narrate the mod's version, author, and description, etc
- When selecting the config button, the narrator narrates only the word "Button", until it begins to narrate the tooltip after narrating the guide.
- Cannot use the keyboard to scroll the description area.

issues.title: Provided screen factories causing unnecessary overhead when opening mod menu screen
issues.body: I'm currently using the API to provide config screens for other mods. As stated by the docs, I need to return a map of all the mods ids and their associated config screen factory. However `ModMenuApi#getProvidedConfigScreenFactories` is being called for every mod and library, and this means my provider is running 46 times at minimum (Fabric, it's libraries, and Mod Menu). My suggestion would be to call `getProvidedConfigScreenFactories` from each provider once, combine them and then request from that map.

issues.title: Better config exception handling
issues.body:
Currently, if a mod's config screen factory generation failed, the button simply disappears.

For UX, this is very bad as users then become confused why a certain mod no longer has a button to open config. Instead, the button should just disable itself with a tooltip explaining the problem.

issues.title: Update notifications should not be shown for hidden mods
issues.body:
Mods button should not show the diamond on the button if the updatable mod is deliberately hidden (but may not be deliberately excluded from updates) or is a library and libraries are hidden.

Case in point: mods button showed a diamond for Fabric API, which is a library and I have libraries hidden on list.
Tested on 5.1.0-beta.4 for 1.19.3.

issues.title: ModMenu thinks v2.6.10 on Modrinth is newer than v2.6.11 (Also on Modrinth)
issues.body:
ModMenu's update check doesn't seem to be that good or accurate as it tells me that the mod "Fast Load" has a new update available on Modrinth.
The update in question is v2.6.10 (Or `v1.19.3.fabric.2.6.10` as it is shown), which obviosuly isn't newer than 2.6.11 which is installed.

I think ModMenu thinks it's newer because the latest version for the loader (Fabric) is set to 2.6.11, while the previous version is set as `1.19.3.fabric.2.6.10`.

Idk if there would be a fix for this, but perhaps a tool like FlexVer should be used for comparing versions, as it usually is capable of recognizing different version patterns like the above and properly determine if the version is actually new or not.

Screenshot:
![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11576465/219690751-4edd877f-986d-46a5-9c5f-e9c8a873ef6c.png)

issues.title: Split hidden mod and config button config
issues.body:
As a modpack maintainer, I'd like to force a list of hidden mods and config buttons, but other settings can just be set as defaults without needing to force them every time (e.g. with [YOSBR](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/yosbr))

This could be done if Mod Menu split its config into two files.

issues.title: Modpack update checker
issues.body:
As #84 got finally merged, I started wondering if that could be reused for modpacks.

Flow: 
1. The modpack author enters their Modrinth pack URL and current version (for point of comparison) in Mod Menu config
2. Update prompts should appear somewhere in title screen as toasts/icon/label
3. Ideally, when the option is enabled, Mod Menu should not check for updates of mods that are contained in the modpack (so only check for mods that are not, which the user probably added themselves). If that's too hard, I'd just disable the mod checker in my modpack altogether so that people would download modpack updates as a whole.
4. Also I'd prefer if people were not able to "click" anything and get led to the listing, but rather just nudge them to update via their launcher's methods instead.

See also: #126

issues.title: Filter to just mods with configuration available
issues.body:
As modpack developers, we like to provide instructions on how to configure some mods in our modpack documentation, which means players need to find their way to the configuration menu, and the more concise those instructions can be the better.

We've previously used [modsettings](https://github.com/magicus/ModSettings) for this, but found that modmenu has more compatibility support, and the richer interface is easier to use for long modlists. 

Our instructions are often things like `ALT+M->Ears`, and with the new modmenu keybind it's pretty close, but It'd help if there was a configurable-mods-only filter (that we could then set as default in the modmenu config)

issues.title: Load mod-defined resources earlier
issues.body:
Mod Menu has an API for mods, which, among other things contains translatable descriptions and summaries.

A year ago I discovered that most mods actually don't use the summaries, which gave me a creative idea - what if I made a resource pack for my modpack to make all summaries consistent? [So I did](https://github.com/Fabulously-Optimized/fabulously-optimized/tree/main/Mod%20Menu%20Helper), people liked it and contributed translations to it.

However, recently some modders and translators have discovered the feature, and due to the way Mod Menu loads these strings later than the resource packs, the resource pack string becomes useless for those mods. 

So here is my suggestion: **what if you loaded mod-defined descriptions and summaries earlier than the resource packs?** It would then work similarly to how resource packs can change a mod's textures. 

Related to #401

issues.title: Translation improvement ideas
issues.body:
As recommended in https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/issues/450#issuecomment-1152964684 do I now open this issue in the hopes to start a discussion on possible improvements towards the current source strings for translations.

Right now, I see 2 minor problems that I think should be improved.

#### 1. Usage of past tense in translations

This may depend on the actual translations done but the usage of past tense such as `Shown` or `Hidden` feels... Odd.
Sure Minecraft itself uses `Shown` in some of its settings, but it still doesn't mean it sounds or feels right.
I personally believe that the usage of `Show` and `Hide` would also work too.

At least for translations such as german should the present tense be used because `Gezeigt` sounds seriously stupid.

#### 2. Condense option values

There are a lot of duplicate values in the source String. I already mentioned two: `Shown` and `Hidden`.
I feel like there is no need to have separate entries for each option that has the exact same values. Sure, you can come up with the argument that a language may use a different word/character/... for this particular combination, but how likely is that? Can anyone that is translating any of the currently offered languages list such a situation for this mod?

It would benefit both sides for sure to have less duplicate text. Devs have less lines to maintain and translators don't have to repeat the same sentence/word x times.

issues.title: Add support to open the mod's config without Mod Menu's dependency
issues.body:
As the title says, it would be nice if I didn't have to bundle Mod Menu as a dependency just to show the configuration menu while not really using other features.

The main reason why I mention this is because I typically don't like adding libraries to my mods if they aren't really used by the mod itself as that only creates unwanted dependencies.

My thought so far is to use the same way as one would do when wanting to add a config screen but instead of using `ModMenuApi` as the implementing interface, one can use `Function<Screen, Screen>` (or `UnaryOperator<Screen>`) where the first `Screen` type represents the previous screen and the second `Screen` represents the "config" screen. Instead of using `getModConfigScreenFactory()`, `apply(Screen)` is used instead.

issues.title: [Request] Show `suggests`/`recommends` entries and allow for more info in `"custom": {"modmenu": {`
issues.body:
Currently the `"suggests"` and `"recommends"` entries in `fabric.mod.json` don't do much of anything (`"recommends"` just spams the log a little). 

It would be great if Mod Menu showed these things to users. 

If only the `"suggests"` and/or `"recommends"` entries are present, a simple list of their mod ids could be shown. 

For more info, mod makers could put an `"optional_dependencies"` array in `"custom": {"modmenu": {` (or just use `"suggests"`/`"recommends"` again in there).

This could let them specify things like mod name and mod home page, in addition to providing a summary of why the mod is recommended. 

If the entry in `"custom": {"modmenu": {` were present, the `"suggests"`/`"recommends"` entries in `fabric.mod.json` would be ignored.

issues.title: Question: ModMenu build dependency
Suggestion: Give users the option to hide/unhide mods
issues.body:
I'd like to suggest to add a feature that allows users to manually hide/unhide mods from the Mod Menu.

Just like we can make Mods visible that are hidden, it would be nice if we were able hide certain mods ourselves. Say you run the game with certain "main mods" which you're always using and that are set to our liking, hiding them would help with keeping a better overview of new/other/testing/... mods to only see them.

It could be as simple as offering clickable check boxes to mark the mods which we want to hide and at the next time mod menu gets opened, they are hidden. To see them again we can simply switch to show hidden mods (including those automatically hidden) to make them visible again and thus to remove the checkmark if we want to permanently unhide them again.

Or it could be more sophisticated by adding a whole new listing of the installed mods that allows us to mark/un-mark those mods we'd like to hide/unhide. But I don't think that would be necessary - the most simple integration of such a feature would be enough (for me at least).

Thanks for considering.

issues.title: Provide clear instructions for devs to update deprecated features and fix warnings

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: This could be resolved quicker with help

issues.body:
This is related to #231 and several other related requests regarding API changes and deprecations.

Currently we have this scenario:
- ModMenu introduces a new feature / API change.
- The old API is marked deprecated and a WARNING is emitted, saying _"ask the author of this mod to support the new API"_
- Users see the warnings and promptly ask authors to fix
- Many authors resist to fix, for several reasons:
  - They don't know _how_ to fix
  - Don't have the time/willingness to study the new API and update
  - "If ain't broke I don't care", or "That's ModMenu's fault for constantly changing the API"
- Users start complaining with ModMenu, creating issues and requesting warnings to be disabled, grouped, etc

ModMenu could minimize or even solve all this by making it _dead easy_ to update to the new API. For Authors, and even users to submit a PR.

In every deprecation Warning, add a link to a wiki page that explains _that exact change and precisely what needs to be done to update_. So users can ask authors: "Could you please support the new API _by following the instructions here_?". Or better: "Here's a PR that implements the changes described at ...". That's _much_ better than a "please fix this" request that demands authors to take their time.

Example: the infamous `modmenu:clientsideOnly' custom value` deprecation warning.

 How to fix it? _Where_ to fix it? Should I just remove that block/line, or are there additional changes required? The wiki only gives subtle clues:
> There are more badges, such as the Client badge, but this is automatically determined by the environment defined in the official fabric.mod.json metadata

Oh, ok, so we need to edit `fabric.mod.json`. Cool. So we do as #300 did and remove the custom block. But... what about this "determined by the environment"? How/Where do I set this? Where is this documented? Wiki does not mention it. Granted, this is a general Fabric setting, not part of the ModMenu API. But still, more research is needed to make sure we set `environment` to `client` (is that a plain key-value? A new group? In the same file?)

See the problem?

Please, if you guys want new API to be supported, without adding tension between users and authors, for every deprecation warning create a Wiki page instructing exactly where and what should be changed. Add code snippets for the common cases. Lower the barrier for adoption as low as you possibly can.

issues.title: If a mod that doesn't specify an icon is present, the log can be spammed

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: This could be resolved quicker with help

issues.body:
The fabric.mod.json spec specifies that `icon` is an optional field, therefore, not specifying an icon should be fine.

However, if a mod doesn't contain the `icon` key in the fabric.mod.json file, ModMenu will print a warning to the log not only once or when opening the menu, but also every time a mod that can be collapsed is collapsed or expanded (it doesn't have to be the "faulty" one).

```log
[14:25:16] [Render thread/WARN] (Mod Menu) Warning! Mod modid has a broken icon, loading default icon
```

issues.title: Single-sided mods
issues.body:
Hello, I'm the developer and maintainer of a mod called [Fabric Console](https://github.com/LoganDark/fabric-console). I'm currently bringing the project up to date, which means I've updated Mod Menu to the latest 1.16 version (for now), 1.16.22.

It seems that the mod now lacks the option to specify a mod as client-side-only if it also supports the server, which _does_ make sense. However, Fabric Console _is_ purely a single-sided mod - it adds no new content, and simply allows for color in the console (dedicated server or client alike). In this case I still feel it's important to be able to articulate the fact that it is not required for both server & client to have this mod installed.

I propose a new custom field (name TBD) to specify that a mod requires no interaction between client & server. This would replace the "modmenu:clientsideOnly" field that is being deprecated & removed soon.

issues.title: 1.17.1 Compatibility
issues.body:
Quite a few mod developers include ModMenu as a dependency in CurseForge for Minecraft 1.17.1 but as ModMenu does not have any files marked as compatible with 1.17.1, including any of these mods in a modpack will make an old version of ModMenu install which is not compatible with Minecraft 1.17.1, breaking modpacks until the original mod which apparently depends on ModMenu is removed. 

Please Could you mark the 1.17 versions of ModMenu (at least the one's which are compatible) as being compatible with Minecraft 1.17.1 so that it fixes all these mods, and also allows users to include your mod in their modpacks :)

issues.title: Allow declaration and configuration of config button
issues.body: Currently, the config button presence relies on invoking the screen factory and checking for a non-null reference. I would like to have a button present without a screen and have control over that button to define a ClickEvent that opens my mod's respective config file. The non-null check could be moved to a dedicated method, and that method could be delegated to from a new API method that creates the button component.

issues.title: [Suggestion] Add the functionality to "activate" and "de-activate" mods
issues.body:
Having to drag out and back in mods when we do or don't need them can get annoying. How about adding a feature to your mod that not only allows as to take a look at all the mods currently running but also to select which of them should run and which shouldn't.

Maybe this could be done by automatically changing certain parts of the mods' code to remarks or by temporarily renaming the mods file format (to make them not work upon restart) or by telling the game to ignore certain files... I really don't know, I'm just blindly guessing as I'm not a coder. So I don't know if this would technically even be possible and if so, how. I just wanted to suggest it for you to consider possibly adding it.

issues.title: Show people-specific contact info

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: This could be resolved quicker with help

issues.body:
The fabric.mod.json spec indicates that authors and contributors can be Person objects. While very rarely (if at all!) is it used, it would be useful to get contact info for someone specific from the menu itself.

I'd like this feature because I don't have one discord server and I kind of don't want to make one because I don't push my name out there much (should probably work on that) and so it's probably better to add contact info for myself rather than about the mod itself. Additionally, it would help improve compat with the spec.

issues.title: Default getModId implementation crashes the game - ModMenu 1.10.5 for 1.15.2
issues.body:
When the game loads, it will crash if getModId returns null, which is now the default implementation.
https://paste.ubuntu.com/p/mR5ybQz7h8/
The crash seems to come from [here](https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/blob/1.15/src/main/java/io/github/prospector/modmenu/ModMenu.java#L72), because the ImmutableMap doesn't like null keys (And from the documentation I wouldn't expect it to be added as a null key either based on the documentation, which [says the modid will be pulled from the loader](https://github.com/TerraformersMC/ModMenu/blob/1.15/src/main/java/io/github/prospector/modmenu/api/ModMenuApi.java#L42).

Basically like many file explorers.

issues.title: Formatted Text Capabilities
issues.body:
I would really like the ability to define formatted text in my summary/description. By formatted text I basically mean a text component with support for things like fonts, sub components, links, click events, etc. 

To give a use case I have a mod which registers a new vanilla compatible font. I would like to include a message written in this font inside my description. This would serve as a showcase of the font and also provide a very effective way to verify that the font is registered and working.

This could ideally be implemented using Text.Serializer's deserializer method which would support the full feature range via json objects. No idea where this would fit into the spec though.

issues.title: More flexible badges
issues.body:
A proposal regarding the badge system:

 - replace the `BadgeType` enum with a `BadgeType` class which stores: `Text text`, `int outlineColor`, `int fillColor`, and `Predicate<ModMetadata> predicate`.
 - add a Badge registry, which holds a list of `BadgeType`s
 - add a `Collection<BadgeType> getModBadgeTypes()` to `ModMenuApi`, and hook it up to the badge registry
 - instead of the current hardcoded logic in `BadgeRenderer`, just do something equivalent to `BadgeRegistry.getBadgeTypes().stream().filter(badge -> badge.predicate.test(metadata)).forEach(badge -> drawBadge(matrices, badge, mouseX, mouseY))`
 
This would allow mods to add their own badge types, which could be useful for e.g. Patchwork-type projects without having to hardcode them all.

issues.title: Add config options to mod count
issues.body: In fabric.mod.json, you can specify for a mod to parent another mod to make everything look nicer (seen below) with "modmenu:parent". The issue with this is that the sub-mod/child mod is not counted in the total number of mods, even though it should (in my opinion), because although it is an extension to the mod, it is still a mod in of itself, and many people (in my experience) use ModMenu to quickly check if the new mod they're using works, and if the number has not gone up, it may be a hassle to manually check if it is just a sub mod and has not been counted, or if there's a mod incompatibility issue or smth.

issues.title: If a mod's name starts with a lowercase letter, the mod is sent to the bottom.
issues.body: If a mod's name starts with a lowercase letter, the mod is sent to the bottom (in ModMenu), breaking alphabetical order. I've had to manually modify fabric.mod.json if multiple mods and have to submit a pull request to fix this. It would be logical for it to still be displayed in alphabetical order correctly, and even nicer (but not strictly necessary) if it was automatically capitalised so that it didn't trigger me to be the odd one/two out.

issues.title: The ability to manually mark mods as libraries
issues.body: Some library mods don't have the tag, and it would be nice to be able to manually hide them.

issues.title: Better client-side mod detection
issues.body: Currently, the only way to have mod menu show a mod as client-side is to add the `modmenu:clientsideOnly` tag to fabric.mod.json. However, client-side-only mods _should_ already be using `"environment": "client"` so as to not load on dedicated servers. It seems like a no-brainer to have mod menu simply detect that rather than requiring mods to add a custom tag (you can keep the tag of course, this request is simply additive).

issues.title: Take advantage of new entrypoint containers in fabric-loader
issues.body:

issues.title: Crash when Mod Menu screen re-inits with an empty list
issues.body:
**Affected versions:**
Up to 1.7.8+build.117

**Steps to reproduce:**
* Open ModMenu gui
* Turn on libraries if you have to to get a gui with a config
* Click on a library which has a config and a working Done / back button. LibGui has such a button.
* Type into the search bar until no mods are showing
* Go into the config of the mod you had selected
* Hit "Done" or back out of the config to the ModMenu Screen

**Expected result:**
ModMenu screen appears, and either the search box is cleared or the interface looks the same way we left it

**Observed result:**
Hard crash as ModMenu appears to look up the selected item from the [empty] list.
https://gist.github.com/falkreon/265cfe5edcc8eb10023a6ea64cb0d9e3

issues.title: Crash when pressing F3 + Esc

labels.name: implemented
labels.description: This has been added to the project

issues.body:
WHen pressing `F3 + Esc` (pause the game without visible screen in singleplayer) the game crasehs due to ModMenu's mixin trying to access index 5 of an empty array list.

I encountered the issue in AOF first, and was able to reproduce it in my dev workspace:
```
java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: 5, Size: 0
	at java.util.ArrayList.rangeCheckForAdd(ArrayList.java:665) ~[?:1.8.0_212]
	at java.util.ArrayList.add(ArrayList.java:477) ~[?:1.8.0_212]
	at net.minecraft.client.gui.screen.GameMenuScreen.addButton(GameMenuScreen.java:534) ~[minecraft-1.14.4-mapped-net.fabricmc.yarn-5.jar:?]
	at net.minecraft.client.gui.screen.GameMenuScreen.handler$drawMenuButton$zep001(GameMenuScreen.java:527) ~[minecraft-1.14.4-mapped-net.fabricmc.yarn-5.jar:?]
```

which leads to this line in the mixin output:
```java
    @MixinMerged(
        mixin = "io.github.prospector.modmenu.mixin.PauseMenuScreenMixin",
        priority = 1000,
        sessionId = "e4704896-c392-449d-8fc2-5270d7798be2"
    )
```

issues.title: [Feature Request] Customizable per-mod backgrounds
issues.body:
Let mods optionally change the background of the mod menu if it is currently selected, by providing images in a 'background' folder/package near the mod icon

**Why**: 
That could allow mods to provide 'hints' (ex. screenshots of new worlds, entities, blocks...) for the user about the mod without visiting the mod homepage/wiki. Although that would be irrelevant in self-made modpacks or with just a few mods, it would enhance modpacks with tons of mods.
